desktop.account.address.label: Address — this account's X25519 public key, standard base64
desktop.account.fact.noPush.body: There is no push on desktop (PARITY.md row 2.3). This client POLLS /v2/messages and the call server: calls and messages arrive only while the process is running, and the poll interval is the delivery latency. Closing the window keeps OSHI running in the menu bar or tray; Quit stops it. Nothing wakes it from sleep — turn on Open at login under More so it is running after a restart.
desktop.account.fact.noPush.title: Delivery stops when OSHI quits
desktop.account.fact.plaintext.body: Each message record is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a dedicated history key held by the OS-backed vault (or its explicit passphrase fallback). Older local journals are upgraded atomically when opened. An unlocked OSHI session can still read its own history.
desktop.account.fact.plaintext.title: History on this disk is encrypted
desktop.account.gate.closed.value: CLOSED — sends are refused before they reach the network (PARITY.md row 0.8)
desktop.account.gate.label: V2 rollout gate
desktop.account.gate.open.value: OPEN — this account may publish a prekey bundle and send

desktop.empty.conversations.body: A conversation appears here the first time a message is sent or received. Nothing was announced to any server to get you this far.
desktop.empty.conversations.footnote: Those are REPL commands: ./oshi.sh run --args="--client". This window has no contact picker or live camera scanner, but New → Scan QR image accepts a saved QR code from your phone.
desktop.empty.conversations.step1.detail: /qr prints this account's key as text or a PNG.
desktop.empty.conversations.step1.title: Show your own code
desktop.empty.conversations.step2.detail: They add it on their phone; nothing is published.
desktop.empty.conversations.step2.title: Give it to the other person
desktop.empty.conversations.step3.detail: /send <address> <text> in the REPL, then it opens here.
desktop.empty.conversations.step3.title: Send the first message
desktop.empty.groups.body: A group appears here when you are added to one, or when you create one with /group new in the REPL. Sending into a group DOES work from this window: a message is fanned out over one ratchet session per member, and the outcome line says how many of them took it.
desktop.empty.matches.body: Nothing in this list contains “%@”. This box filters the conversations already on screen — it does not search inside message history.
desktop.export.card.body: An export holds every conversation on this computer, encrypted with this account's key. Only an OSHI session holding the same account (restored with its recovery key) can open it. Nothing is written unencrypted.

desktop.export.error.otherAccount: This export belongs to another OSHI account. Restore that account's key first.

desktop.limits.intro: The macOS app has 102 screens (VIEWS.md). This window implements a handful. Rather than let absence be ambiguous, everything below is named with the reason and the PARITY.md row behind it.
desktop.limits.missing.heading: NOT AVAILABLE IN THIS CLIENT

desktop.limits.notYet.note: A schedule, not a limit. Every one of these is reachable today from the REPL: ./oshi.sh run --args="--client"

desktop.nickname.body: Shown to your contacts instead of your address. It travels inside your encrypted profile update and never notifies anyone. A name you give a contact yourself always wins over the one they chose.
desktop.nickname.cleared: Nickname removed. %d of %d contact(s) were told.
desktop.nickname.pull.none: Your phone's profile archive holds no nickname.
desktop.nickname.pushed: Nickname written to the encrypted profile archive your phones read. Their avatar and links were kept.
desktop.nickname.saved: Nickname saved and sent to %d of %d contact(s).
desktop.nickname.sync.hint: Your phones share the nickname through their encrypted profile archive. This only reaches them when this computer holds the same account (restored with its recovery key).
desktop.nickname.title: Your nickname
desktop.nickname.withheld: Saved on this computer only. It is not sent to your contacts from here, because this computer holds your phone's account and a profile sent from it would replace what your phone tells them. Set the nickname on your phone, or use Send to my phone.
desktop.noConversation.count: Conversations on this disk: %d. Everything you see comes from those files — this window has no sample data and no placeholder threads.
desktop.noConversation.empty: There is nothing on this disk yet. The panel on the left has the three steps.
desktop.noConversation.title: Pick a conversation
desktop.safety.verify.hint: Paste the other person's SAFETY:v1 QR payload. This checks the exact keys, not just the digits.
desktop.safety.verify.mismatch: The QR payload does not match this contact's identity.
desktop.thread.empty.bot: This lane has no encryption at all, which is why it has no composer here.
desktop.thread.empty.group: Group messages are listed here when they arrive. Sending one from this window is not wired yet — PARITY.md row 0.17.
desktop.thread.empty.lora: Stock Meshtastic text, quarantined and flagged unverified — PARITY.md row 0.27.
desktop.background.title: Calls and messages in the background
desktop.background.body: Closing the window keeps OSHI running in the menu bar or tray, so calls ring and messages arrive. Quit from that icon to stop it. A computer has no push service for OSHI: nothing reaches this machine while OSHI is not running.
desktop.background.login: Open OSHI at login (in the background)
